back: A structured set of financial and non-financial performance indicators useful to managers, and the values these indicators assume over a defined period.
Balanced · long-term perspective · in line with strategy · facilitate decision-making
Indicators must be preceded by a performance model; include indicators for goals AND main lines of action. Never just list indicators and pick.
Focus attention on a few priorities: few indicators, monitored directly and systematically by managers, changing frequently.
Ensure the organisation is under control: more, varied, balanced indicators; recurrent; pre-established values → only abnormal deviations escalated; controllers heavily involved.
Separate dashboards per use are unusual – one dashboard usually serves several functions (boosting + reporting, or monitoring + reporting). Any indicator can serve any use.
Dashboard method by M. Fiol & H. Jordan linking Objectives (O), Critical Performance Variables / Variables d'Action (VA) and Responsibilities (R).
Double-entry table of priority objectives × critical performance variables; crosses show causal links. No predefined framework for the content (unlike the strategy map).
Name of the main lines of action in the OVAR method.
Restricted meaning: only the operational translation of a goal (lines of action are the CPVs).
Quantifies an objective by directly capturing the expected result.
Quantifies an objective by focusing on the means / levers adopted to achieve it.
Formulation of objectives · causal links · linking an objective to several others · two levels (expected results & action levers).
Delivers indicators within a short timeframe, in an easily readable form (graphs, colour codes …).
